references.text: Abraham says almost identical words: 'The Lord, the God of heaven, who took me from my father's house and from my native land, and who spoke to me and swore, "I will give this land to your offspring"—he will send his angel before you, so that you may get a wife for my son from there.'
God says to Abraham: 'Walk before me and be blameless.' This is the direct background for Abraham's words in 24:40: 'The Lord, before whom I have walked.'

Jacob speaks of God as his shepherd throughout his life, and the angel who has rescued him from all harm. The combination of walking before God's face and the angel's protection reflects Genesis 24:40.

Jacob promises faithfulness to God if God will be with him and keep him on his way—a similar trust in God's guidance and protection on the journey, as seen in Abraham's words that God will send his angel.
God promises to send his angel before the people to lead them on their way—a direct parallel to Abraham's promise that God will send his angel with the servant.
Enoch walked with God—an early example of the expression 'to walk before/with God's face' which Abraham uses about himself in 24:40.
Narrative connection: Verse 40 is the prophecy that the journey will succeed, while verse 56 confirms that this promise has been fulfilled.
Instruction and mission guarantee: Verse 4 gives the mission; the source verse explains the divine mechanism (the angel of the Lord) that will ensure its execution.
Theological parallel: Both verses confirm that the angel of the Lord goes before to lead God's people to their destination.
Theological parallel: Both verses illustrate God's practice of sending an angel to guide or reveal His will to His servants.
Prophetic forerunner: The 'angel of the Lord' as a guide in the source verse foreshadows Malachi's 'messenger of the covenant' who prepares the way for the Lord.
Theological parallel: Both verses show the 'angel of the Lord' as the active agent carrying out God's plans (guidance versus revelation).
Theological parallel: Both verses concern a divine messenger preparing the way for God's plans (guidance versus messianic preparation).
